BOOGIE-WOOGIE — Chicago 1928. Clarence "Pine Top" Smith cut
"Pine Top's Boogie Woogie" for Vocalion in December 1928 — the
record that NAMED the music, with Smith talking the dancers
through the breaks over that rolling left hand. THREE rows have
wanted this by name since their lineages were written — `blues`,
`rocknroll` and `jumpblues`, which is the census's own top want
— because the eight-to-the-bar left hand is where the shuffle,
the walking eighths and half of rock and roll's right hand come
from. All three take it as a parent today.
THE AXES: TIME and CAST. One player, two hands, and the left one
IS the rhythm section — said below as the bass chair walking
eighths under a kit that is one empty object, because a rent
party had a piano and no drummer.

the row's own words: "One player, two hands"

LINEAGE: `ragtime` (Sedalia 1899) is the professional piano
tradition this is the rough cousin of; the barrelhouses and
lumber camps that actually taught the left hand are named
below — a debt with no named record until this one.

THE MODE THIS RECORD CANNOT SOUND (2026-09-02, the catalogue round,
shift 2; test/precompose.test.js G14b).
Clarence "Pine Top" Smith, "Pine Top's Boogie Woogie" (Vocalion, Chicago,
December 1928) — this row's own record, the one that named the music. The
eight-to-the-bar left hand walks a major-key twelve bars; the roots above
are degrees 0, 3 and 4 and never 6. See `zydeco` for the full ruling; the
blue seventh stays where it lives, in SCALES.blues on this line.

THE SWING IS THE LINE'S; THERE IS NO DRUMMER TO SWING (2026-09-05, the swing
census). This row renders NO drum event at all, so its declared swing can
only ever be the players'. MEASURED over the whole record, as written
against `swing` forced to 0: 0 of 0 hits and 2,749 of 10,097 line events
moved at seed 1 (2,101 of 7,717 at seed 2, 2,161 of 10,552 at seed 3). THE
LEFT HAND IS THE RHYTHM SECTION: eight to the bar under a right hand that
answers it, which is exactly why three rows want this one by name. A boogie
pianist is his own drummer, so the shuffle has to live in the line, and the
measurement finds it there. Kept as declared.
